battle.name: 淝水之戰
battle.theater: 淝水壽陽戰線（安徽淮南壽縣）
battle.brief: 公元383年，前秦苻堅傾國南下，東晉以謝玄領北府兵八萬、劉牢之五千前鋒迎戰，戰場在壽陽淝水兩岸。晉軍夜襲洛澗破秦軍前鋒，復隔水誘敵，涉水衝擊秦軍鐵騎並斷其浮橋，秦軍大潰，屍塞淝水。卡面的羅馬標槍未隨軍而至，其短桿投槍工藝與魏晉步兵標槍、北府兵長柄矛同類。

kit.name: 羅馬標槍
kit.history: 半米長的投槍，槍幹中空。捅穿盾之後就折斷，敵人只能帶著半截槍退回掩體。

countries: 淝水之戰是前秦與東晉在壽陽（今安徽淮南壽縣）一線的決定性交鋒，兩方的國家結構、軍隊組成與補給方式幾乎完全相反。前秦是氐族人苻氏建立的政權，苻堅在王猛輔助下先後滅前燕、前涼與代國，於公元376年前後統一北方，兼有巴蜀、梁益與關中之地，兵威直抵江淮；苻堅以氐人為軍隊骨幹，以漢人士族為文治，又自居大單于，統合北方各族。前秦的軍隊是多族混編：關中舊部與苻融、慕容垂等降附的鮮卑、羌、胡將領各領本部，苻堅屢下禁令要求不得虐待降人、不得侮辱其將帥，可見彼此的裂痕隨時可被利用。東晉則是衣冠南渡的漢人政權，由門閥執政，前秦南下的消息傳來時，朝議多以正朔相承、晉主休明為不可伐之由。前秦是主動遠征的一方，東晉是以少量精兵守土的一方：苻堅總攬前鋒、中軍與後續諸路，東晉則由謝安以中書監、錄尚書事總攬朝政，謝石為征討大都督、謝玄為前鋒都督，桓沖都督揚豫江三州諸軍事鎮守姑孰，壽陽守將臧質與水軍主將胡彬分守城池與淮水，劉牢之領精兵五千為先鋒。東晉的補給全在本地，四府屯田與庚戌土斷充實了錢糧；前秦卻要從關中沿石門、汴水、蒗薚渠一路把糧船運到汝潁，涼州兵走到咸陽、巴蜀兵順流而下，都沒能及時抵達戰場。
countriesEn: The Battle of Fei River was the decisive engagement between the Former Qin and the Eastern Jin on the Shouyang line, in what is now Shouxian county of Huainan in Anhui, and the two sides differed almost completely in the structure of their states, in the composition of their armies and in the way they were supplied. The Former Qin was a state founded by the Di people under the Fu surname. With Wang Meng as his minister, Fu Jian destroyed Former Yan, Former Liang and the Dai kingdom in turn, unified the north around the year 376, and held as well Sichuan, the Yi and Liang commanderies and Guanzhong, so that his military power reached as far as the Jiang and the Huai. Fu Jian used the Di as the skeleton of his army and the Chinese literati for his civil administration, and at the same time styled himself the Chanyu and gathered the various peoples of the north under his command. His army was mixed across ethnic lines: the old troops of Guanzhong and the surrendered or subordinate Xianbei, Qiang and Hu commanders such as Fu Rong and Murong Chui each led their own contingents, and Fu Jian had to issue repeated orders forbidding the ill-treatment of surrendered men and the insulting of their officers, which shows only too well that the fissure between them could be exploited at any moment. The Eastern Jin was a Han Chinese state ruled by the great families who had moved south after the Yongjia disaster, and when the news of the Qin advance came, the debate at court turned on the fact that the Jin was the successor to the true calendar and that its ruler was a good one, and could therefore not be attacked. Qin was the side that marched out to attack, the Jin the side that met the attack with a small body of picked troops. Fu Jian commanded the vanguard, the central army and the follow-up columns; in the Jin, Xie An, as Director of the Secretariat and Recorder of the Department of State Affairs, directed the government, Xie Shi was General for the Conquest of the Rebels, Xie Xuan was General of the Vanguard, Huan Chong held the military command of Yang, Yu and Jiang and sat at Gusu, the defender of Shouyang Zang Zhi and the commander of the river forces Hu Bin held the city and the Huai respectively, and Liu Laozhi led five thousand picked men as the advance guard. The Jin drew its supplies entirely from local sources, and the garrison farms of the four provinces together with the Gengxu land settlement had filled its coffers; Qin, by contrast, had to move its grain barges from Guanzhong by way of Shimen, the Bian waterway and the Cangyan canal so as to reach the Ruying. The Liangzhou troops got no further than Xianyang, and the Bashu troops were still coming down the river; neither reached the field in time.
people: 留下姓名的關鍵人物分屬兩方，而秦方的名字幾乎都跟著敗亡一起被記下。苻堅是前秦的皇帝，也是這場戰爭的發動者：他自述「吾統承大業，垂二十載」，在朝議上估計「略計兵仗精卒，可有九十七萬」，又以「以吾之眾旅，投鞭於江足斷其流」自負；當苻融、太子苻宏、中心公苻詵與大和尚道安都反對南伐時，他仍以「以累捷之威，擊垂亡之寇」作答。幕僚王猛的臨終之誡正說中要害：晉雖僻陋吳越，卻是正朔相承、親仁善鄰之國，不可圖，而「鮮卑羌虜，我之仇也，終為人患」。苻堅的同母弟、相國苻融是全軍最清醒的人，他主張兵疲將倦不可伐，力陳關中留守的少卒與畿甸的鮮卑羌羯是國之賊；他統帥二十五萬前鋒，渡淮攻陷壽陽，命梁成率五萬進攻洛澗，最後同意後退半渡、以鐵騎擊敵的方略，卻在軍隊失控時縱馬攔阻，馬倒而死。苻融之弟苻方與苻堅之弟苻雙分兵攻城與宿衛，苻方攻壽陽不下。慕容垂、慕容暐各率數萬眾馳赴鄖城，龍驤將軍姚萇率梁益水陸軍自沔水與長江上游而下，涼州兵團由梁熙統轄；這些秦將此後的選擇，都變成前秦解體的伏筆：苻堅回長安後殺了王統與苻方，慕容垂與姚萇隨即反噬其主。晉方的核心是謝安、謝玄與劉牢之。謝安在朝中總攬五州軍事，力主鎮靜，是「弈棋破敵」典故的主角；謝玄以廣陵為基地多募勁勇，選劉牢之與東海何謙等驍將為參軍，練出號稱「百戰百勝」的北府兵；劉牢之率精兵五千夜渡洛澗、斬梁成，一戰成名。降將朱序的背叛最關鍵：他是襄陽失守後被俘的晉將，戰前奉苻堅之命赴晉營勸降，卻反勸謝石趁秦軍未集速擊，戰中又在陣後高呼「秦軍敗矣」。
peopleEn: The names that survive from this war fall on both sides, but nearly all of the Qin names are recorded together with a collapse. Fu Jian was the emperor of the Former Qin and the man who set the war in motion. He said of himself that he had carried on the great enterprise for nearly twenty years, told the court that the arms and picked soldiers he could muster came to something like 970,000, and vaunted the boast that with such a host he could throw the whips into the river and sever its flow. When Fu Rong, the crown prince Fu Hong, the Lord of the Centre Fu Shun and the great monk Dao'an all argued against the southern campaign, he still answered that a run of victories would crush a state already on its last legs. The dying words of his minister Wang Meng had struck nearer the mark: the Jin, though poor and remote in Wu and Yue, was the state that carried the true calendar and was friendly to its neighbours, and should not be attacked, while the Xianbei, Qiang and Jie were the enemies of the Qin and would in the end be a plague. Fu Jian's half-brother and chancellor Fu Rong was the clearest head in the Qin army. He held that the army was exhausted and the commanders weary and therefore must not be used, and he laid out the danger of leaving only a few weak troops to garrison the capital while the Xianbei, Qiang and Jie were massed in the hinterland like a forest. He commanded the vanguard of 250,000, crossed the Huai and took Shouyang, sent Liang Cheng with 50,000 to attack Luojian, and finally agreed to the plan of giving ground so that the Jin could cross and then be crushed by the armoured cavalry; when the army slipped out of control he rode forward to stop it, his horse fell, and he was killed in the press. Fu Jian's younger brother Fu Fang and his brother Fu Shun took charge of siege and of the palace guard, and Fu Fang could not take Shouyang. Murong Chui and Murong Wei each led several tens of thousands towards Yun city, the General of the Dragon Chariot Yao Chang led the Liang and Yi forces down the Mianshui and the upper Yangtze, and the Liangzhou corps was under the command of Liang Xi. The choices these Qin commanders made afterwards became the seeds of the Qin collapse: back in Chang'an Fu Jian had Wang Tong and Fu Fang killed, and Murong Chui and Yao Chang turned on their own master. At the centre of the Jin side were Xie An, Xie Xuan and Liu Laozhi. Xie An directed the military of the five provinces at court, pressed for calm, and is the man of the story of the chess game won without rising from his seat. Xie Xuan, based at Guangling, recruited the strong and the brave and chose as his staff officers men of mettle such as Liu Laozhi and He Qian of the Eastern Sea, and trained the force that was called the Northern Depot troops and that was never beaten in a hundred battles. Liu Laozhi led five thousand picked men across the Luojian by night, killed Liang Cheng and made his name in a single action. The defection of the surrendered general Zhu Xu mattered most of all: he was a Jin officer captured after Xiangyang fell, and before the battle Fu Jian sent him to the Jin camp to demand surrender, but instead he advised Xie Shi to strike at once while the Qin armies were not yet assembled, and in the fighting he called out behind the Qin lines that the Qin army was beaten.
kits: 卡面這件羅馬標槍（pilum）並沒有出現在壽陽。它是羅馬軍團重裝步兵的標準投射兵器：槍頭為軟鐵製的空心管狀槍幹，插在木柄上，全長約兩米，槍幹部分不足半米；羅馬人把它做成受撞即彎折、折斷後留在盾牌上的形狀，正是為了讓對手無法拔出再用，一名持盾兵往往因此被釘在原地。軍團中每名步兵攜帶數十支輕型標槍，前列士卒另備重型標槍，一支支插在腰後的皮囊裡，開戰時依令擲出；投槍波在數百步內覆蓋敵陣，把對方的盾牌抬高、把隊形打散，再由劍盾兵上前列陣決鬥。東晉在壽陽一線所配的裝備與之同類而不同質：步兵以長柄矛為主，輔以環首刀、弓與弩，弩是東晉水陸軍的骨幹火力，劉備攻漢中曾請弩一萬張，可見弩在南方軍隊的編制中已相當常見；北府兵的甲胄以皮甲、札甲為主，騎兵另有鎧甲，但數量有限。洛澗與淝水之間最關鍵的投射火力其實來自秦軍：前秦步騎以標槍、矛、刀配皮甲，羌、鮮卑騎兵善用弓，長於奔射與衝擊；壽陽攻城戰中秦軍築土山、填壕溝，晉軍則以布袋盛土塞住缺口，這種就地取材的攻城與防禦方式，正是當時技術水平的寫照。運輸方面，秦軍運糧船以萬計，自河經石門、汴水、蒗薚渠轉入汝潁；姚萇所部梁益水陸軍自沔水與長江上游而下，並在巴東受阻。沒有羅馬式投槍兵，卻有同樣依賴投射火力與陣形銳度的兩支軍隊。
kitsEn: The Roman javelin on the card, the pilum, did not appear at Shouyang. It was the standard missile of the heavy infantry of the Roman legions: the head was a hollow tubular shank of soft iron socketed onto a wooden shaft, the whole weapon about two metres long, of which the shank proper was less than half a metre. The Romans shaped it so that it would bend and break on impact and stay in the shield, precisely so that the man facing him could not pull it out and use it again; a shield-bearer was often pinned in place by one. Every legionary carried several dozen light javelins, while the men in the front ranks carried the heavy pilum, a bundle of them stuck in a leather case behind the shield, and they were thrown on command. The volley covered the enemy line at several hundred paces, raising his shields and breaking his formation, after which the sword and shield infantry advanced to close quarters. The equipment of the Eastern Jin on the Shouyang line belonged to the same family but was made of different stuff: the foot carried long-hafted spears as their main weapon, with ring-pommel swords, the bow and the crossbow; the crossbow was the backbone of the Jin's river and land forces, and the fact that Liu Bei asked for ten thousand crossbows when he attacked Hanzhong shows how ordinary the weapon already was in the armament of a southern army. The Northern Depot troops were protected by leather and by lamellar armour, and the cavalry had its own metal harness, but in small numbers. The missile fire that really mattered between Luojian and the Fei River came from the Qin side: the Qin foot and horse carried javelins, spears and knives with leather armour, and the Qiang and Xianbei riders were skilled with the bow, strong in the galloping shot and in the charge. In the siege of Shouyang the Qin built earthen ramps and filled the ditches, while the Jin blocked the breaches with sacks of earth, and that making of do with what lay to hand is an exact description of the technical level of the time. On the logistics side, the grain barges of the Qin were counted in tens of thousands and came from the Yellow River by way of Shimen, the Bian waterway and the Cangyan canal to the Ruying; the Liang and Yi forces of Yao Chang came down the Mianshui and the upper Yangtze and were stopped at Badong. There were no Roman pilum-men here, but there were two armies that depended in the same way on missile fire and on the sharpness of their formations.
tactics: 淝水一戰的經過可以拆成五步。第一步是壽陽的攻城與僵持：秦軍渡過淮水攻壽陽前，苻方等率兵攻城，守將臧質以布袋盛土堵塞秦軍築起的土山與被填的壕溝，相持近一年而城終於陷落，臧質被俘；東晉派去接應的水軍主將胡彬聞壽陽失守，退守硤石，糧道幾乎斷絕。謝玄大軍自東向西推進，在洛澗以東二十五里處停駐。第二步是洛澗的夜襲：十一月，謝玄遣劉牢之率精兵五千赴洛澗，秦將梁成隔洛澗布陣，劉牢之渡水進擊，大破梁成軍並斬梁成，秦軍步騎崩潰爭赴淮水，士卒死者一萬五千人；秦軍的銳氣與糧道同時被切斷，胡彬水軍得以與謝玄會合。第三步是隔水對峙與誘敵：秦軍緊靠淝水西岸布陣，晉軍進到淝水東岸，兩軍隔水相望；苻堅與苻融登壽陽城東望，見晉軍部陣齊整，又望八公山草木搖動，皆以為晉兵，驚覺「此亦勍敵也」，軍中由驕轉懼。謝玄遣使對苻融說：君懸軍深入而置陣逼水，是持久之計而非速戰；若移陣少卻使晉兵得渡而決勝負，豈不更善。秦將主張遏住晉軍不讓上岸，苻堅則定下「但引兵少卻，使之半渡，我以鐵騎蹙而殺之」的方略，苻融同意。第四步是崩潰：苻融指揮軍隊稍退，命令逐層傳下，前鋒一退，中軍繼退，整支大軍再也收不住；晉軍趁勢渡水衝殺，《晉書》記張玄等率敢死之士涉水衝擊秦軍鐵騎，其退路上架設的竹木浮橋亦為晉軍所斷，朱序在陣後高呼「秦軍敗矣」，苻融縱馬攔阻時馬倒而死。第五步是追擊與崩潰擴大：晉軍追出三十多里，秦軍自相蹈藉，蔽野塞川；逃散的士卒聞風聲鶴唳皆以為晉兵且至，晝夜不敢稍息，加以飢凍，死者十之七八，晉軍乘勢收復壽陽。
tacticsEn: The course of the battle at Fei River can be broken into five stages. The first is the siege and the stalemate at Shouyang: before the Qin crossed the Huai they had begun the attack on the city with troops under Fu Fang and others, and the defender Zang Zhi plugged the earthen ramps the Qin had thrown up and the ditches they had filled with sacks of earth; after a stalemate of close to a year the city at last fell and Zang Zhi was taken prisoner. Hu Bin, the Jin commander of the river forces sent to help, fell back to Xias on hearing that Shouyang was lost, and the supply road was very nearly cut. Xie Xuan's main army moved from east to west and halted twenty-five li east of Luojian. The second stage is the night attack at Luojian: in the eleventh month Xie Xuan sent Liu Laozhi with five thousand picked men to Luojian, where the Qin general Liang Cheng had deployed across the river; Liu Laozhi crossed and struck, routed Liang Cheng's army and killed him, and the Qin foot and horse broke up and crowded down towards the Huai with fifteen thousand of their men dead. The morale of the Qin army and its supply line were cut in one stroke, and Hu Bin's river force was able to join Xie Xuan. The third stage is the stand across the water and the drawing of the enemy in: the Qin deployed hard against the western bank of the Fei and the Jin came to the eastern bank, the two armies facing each other across the stream. Fu Jian and Fu Rong climbed the east wall of Shouyang and looked out, saw the Jin deployment drawn up in good order, and then looked at the trees and grass on Mount Bagong and took them for soldiers, so that they realised that this too was a formidable host, and the mood in the Qin camp turned from arrogance to alarm. Xie Xuan sent a messenger to Fu Rong to say: you have hung your army deep inside the country and set your line against the water, which is a plan for a long war and not for a quick one; if you shift back a little and let the Jin cross so as to decide the battle, would that not be better? The Qin generals argued that with so many against so few it was safer to bar the Jin from the bank, but Fu Jian settled on the plan of giving ground until the Jin were half across, when he would crush them with the armoured cavalry, and Fu Rong agreed. The fourth stage is the collapse: Fu Rong gave the order to withdraw and it was passed down tier by tier, the vanguard stepped back, the centre followed, and the whole army could no longer be held together. The Jin crossed at once and struck into them. The Jin Shu records that Zhang Xuan and others led men who were ready to die across the water against the Qin armoured cavalry, and that the bamboo and timber floating bridge the Qin had built on their line of retreat was cut by the Jin; Zhu Xu called out behind the Qin lines that the Qin army was beaten, and Fu Rong, riding forward to stop the rout, had his horse fall and was killed in the press. The fifth stage is the pursuit and the widening of the rout: the Jin pursued for more than thirty li, the Qin army trampled itself, the dead covered the field and dammed the streams; the fugitives heard the wind and the cranes and thought the Jin were still on their heels, dared not rest day or night, and with hunger and cold on top of it, seven or eight in ten of them died. The Jin retook Shouyang.
data: 可核對的數字分三類。第一類是文獻自述與編制：前秦出兵的總數，苻堅在朝議上說「略計兵仗精卒，可有九十七萬」，《晉書》多處記作八十餘萬，通行說法是戎卒六十餘萬、騎兵二十七萬；分路是八月苻融以慕容垂等步騎二十五萬為前鋒先行，苻堅隨後繼發，兵分五路——前鋒（苻融）、主力（苻堅自領，駐項城）、幽冀兵團（主將不詳，開赴彭城）、梁益水陸軍（姚萇領，自沔水與長江上游而下）、涼州兵團（梁熙統轄）。羽林軍三萬人由良家子弟充當，實為長安富人的質子軍，只置於苻堅中軍侍從儀衛，並無戰鬥力。真正在淝水與晉軍交手的，只有苻融的前鋒二十餘萬，其中壽陽一帶或有十餘萬眾，其中氐人當不甚多。東晉方面，謝石為征討大都督、謝玄為前鋒都督，與謝琰、桓伊等率眾八萬，以北府兵為主力；劉牢之領精兵五千為先鋒，壽陽守將臧質所部為城防數千人。第二類是過程中的損失：洛澗之戰秦軍死者一萬五千人；淝水決戰後秦軍自相蹈藉，蔽野塞川，屍首塞滿河道；敗退途中飢凍交加，死者十七八；追擊距離三十多里，洛澗距淝水一線約二十五里，淮水是兩軍的分界。第三類是時間與物資：戰役自383年五月桓沖以十萬荊州兵進攻牽制起，七月苻堅下詔大舉、八月前鋒先行、十月攻陷壽陽、十一月洛澗與淝水先後交鋒；秦軍運糧船以萬計，路線自河經石門、汴水、蒗薚渠轉入汝潁，涼州兵只走到咸陽，巴蜀兵在巴東被晉軍守將擋住。徵兵方式是「民每十丁抽出一丁當兵」，良家子年二十以下有材勇者拜羽林郎。
dataEn: The numbers that can be checked fall into three classes. The first class is what the documents say of themselves and how the armies were organised. For the total of the Qin host, Fu Jian told the court that the arms and picked soldiers he could count came to something like 970,000; the Jin Shu several times says eighty-odd ten-thousands, and the usual reckoning is more than 600,000 infantry with 270,000 horse. The army was divided into five columns. In the eighth month Fu Rong led the vanguard of 250,000 foot and horse, with Murong Chui among them, and Fu Jian followed with the main body; the columns were the vanguard under Fu Rong, the main army led by Fu Jian himself and halted at Xiangcheng, a corps of Yougui troops of unknown commander who moved towards Pengcheng, the Liang and Yi water and land forces under Yao Chang who came down the Mianshui and the upper Yangtze, and the Liangzhou corps under Liang Xi. The Feather Forest Guard of 30,000 was made up of well-born sons of the gentry, and was in effect a hostage army of the rich of Chang'an, placed in Fu Jian's central command as escort and ceremonial guard, with no fighting value. Only the vanguard of more than 200,000 under Fu Rong actually engaged the Jin at Fei River, and of the troops at Shouyang it may have been something over 100,000, among whom the Di were by no means the majority. On the Jin side, Xie Shi was General for the Conquest of the Rebels and Xie Xuan General of the Vanguard, and with Xie Yan, Huan Yi and others they brought 80,000 men, the Northern Depot troops being the core; Liu Laozhi led five thousand picked men as the advance guard, and the defenders of Shouyang under Zang Zhi were a few thousand. The second class is the losses in the course of the action: at Luojian the Qin lost fifteen thousand men dead; after the decision at Fei River they trampled one another, the dead covered the field and dammed the streams; on the way back, with hunger and cold, seven or eight in ten perished; the pursuit covered more than thirty li, and Luojian lay about twenty-five li from the Fei line, the Huai being the boundary between the two armies. The third class is time and supplies: the campaign opened in the fifth month of 383 with Huan Chong attacking with 100,000 Jingzhou troops to hold the Qin in check, followed in the seventh month by Fu Jian's edict for the general levy, the advance in the eighth, the fall of Shouyang in the tenth, and the fighting at Luojian and Fei River in the eleventh. The Qin grain barges were counted in tens of thousands and ran from the Yellow River by way of Shimen, the Bian waterway and the Cangyan canal to the Ruying; the Liangzhou troops reached only Xianyang, and the Bashu troops were stopped at Badong by a Jin commander. The levy itself worked on the rule that one man in every ten of the people was taken for the army, and that sons of good families under twenty years of age with talent and strength were enrolled as officers of the Feather Forest.
cause: 打起來的原因有遠近幾層。最遠的一層是前秦的國策：苻堅滅燕之後沒有屠殺燕主與燕國公卿，答覆苻融時說「方將混六合以一家，同有形於赤子」，要把被征服的各族貴族納入同一個國家；這套想法在關中執行了十餘年，到382年基本完成。眼前的觸發點是苻堅本人對南方一廂情願的統一觀念：他不斷用兵，認為「惟東南一隅，未賓王化」，遂於383年七月下詔大舉，民每十丁抽一丁當兵，良家子弟拜羽林郎，傾國而出。直接導致敗因的，是苻堅不肯聽的反對意見。苻融、太子苻宏、中心公苻詵與大和尚道安都說不可伐，苻融的理由有三：歲星在斗牛、吳越得其福，晉主休明而朝臣用命，前秦連年征戰兵疲將倦；更深的一條來自王猛的臨終話語與苻堅自己的答覆：王猛說晉雖僻陋吳越，卻是正朔相承、親仁善鄰之國，不可圖，而「鮮卑羌虜，我之仇也，終為人患，宜漸除之」；苻堅卻以「吾終不以賊遺子孫，為宗廟社稷之憂也」自解，理由是前秦連勝而東晉垂亡，並且真心打算以懷柔統合南方。制度層面的原因則是前秦的兵制：降附的鮮卑、羌、羯各領本部、各自擁兵，關中舊部與降人之間互不信任，苻堅屢下禁令「近收降卒，皆吾秦人，慎勿殺之」，而固有的宿怨仍在。同時前秦的遠征結構本身就有致命裂縫——五路大軍分散在數千里的線上，涼州兵到不了、巴蜀兵被阻、幽冀兵在彭城無用，真正作戰的只有孤立的二十五萬前鋒，後續力量懸隔；而東晉以八萬北府兵在本地作戰，補給線短到幾乎不存在，又有可用之將。苻融當年就警告過：傾國而去，若有風塵之變，其如宗廟何。
causeEn: The reasons for the war lie at several removes. The most distant is the policy of the Former Qin. After destroying Former Yan, Fu Jian did not slaughter the Yan ruler or his court; answering Fu Rong he said that he meant to bring the six quarters together as one family and to treat all alike as children, and to bring the conquered nobles of every people into a single state. That idea had been carried out in Guanzhong for more than a decade and was by 382 all but complete. The immediate trigger is Fu Jian's own one-sided conception of unification in the south: he had used the sword continuously, he held that only one corner in the southeast had not yet been brought under the king's teaching, and so in the seventh month of 383 he issued the edict for the general levy, one man in ten of the people taken for the army, well-born sons of good families enrolled as officers, and put the whole realm into the field. What directly caused the defeat was the advice he refused to take. Fu Rong, the crown prince Fu Hong, the Lord of the Centre Fu Shun and the great monk Dao'an all held that the attack must not be made, and Fu Rong gave three reasons: the year-star stood in Dipper and Ox, which was a blessing for Wu and Yue; the ruler of the Jin was enlightened and his ministers served faithfully; and the Qin had fought many wars and its soldiers and generals were weary. The deeper reason came from the dying words of Wang Meng and from Fu Jian's own reply to them: Wang Meng said that though the Jin was poor and remote in Wu and Yue it carried the true calendar and was friendly to its neighbours and should not be plotted against, and that the Xianbei, Qiang and Jie were the enemies of the Qin and would in the end be a plague and should be removed by degrees; Fu Jian excused himself with the words that he would not leave the enemy to his sons and grandsons to be a danger to the ancestral temple and the altars of state, on the ground that the Qin had the run of victories and the Jin was a dying state, and he genuinely meant to bring the south in through kindness. The reason at the level of institutions lies in the Qin system of war: the surrendered Xianbei, Qiang and Jie each led their own people and their own armed bands, the old troops of Guanzhong and the surrendered men did not trust one another, and Fu Jian had to keep issuing the order that the surrendered soldiers taken recently were all Qin men and must not be killed. Old feuds remained. At the same time the structure of the expedition itself had a fatal flaw in it: the five columns were spread over thousands of li, the Liangzhou troops could not arrive, the Bashu troops were stopped, the Yougui troops were useless at Pengcheng, and the only force that fought was the isolated vanguard of 250,000 with no reliable support behind it. The Jin, by contrast, fought with 80,000 Northern Depot troops on their own ground, with a supply line so short it was almost absent, and with generals who were actually good. Fu Rong had warned in the year itself: if the whole realm leaves and anything stirs in the wind, what will become of the ancestral temple.
impact: 淝水之戰的後果不止於一場會戰的勝負。它首先改變了南北的力量對比：東晉乘勝北伐，一度收回黃河以南故土，鋒芒甚至抵達灞上、潼關；但謝安、謝玄相繼謝世退隱，桓溫、劉裕的北伐消耗了東晉的家底，南北對峙的格局又恢復原狀。其次，前秦在兩年之內解體：苻堅退回長安後聽信讒言殺了王統與苻方，385年苻堅被姚萇所殺，北方先後分裂為後秦、後燕、西秦、代國等，直到439年北魏重新統一北方，才為589年隋朝統一南北舖平了道路；在此之前，北方經歷了近六十年的十六國亂局，漢人與少數族群在戰亂與強制移民中反覆混居，族群融合加速，隋唐關中與山東兩大集團的對立與關洛之爭都源於這一段。制度上，北府兵成為南朝最精銳的武裝，劉牢之、劉裕都以北府兵為崛起之本，南朝軍制的面貌由此定型，荊州桓氏的兵權則在桓玄手上被消耗殆盡。文化上，這場戰役製造了漢語裡最密集的一批成語：投鞭斷流、草木皆兵、風聲鶴唳、踉蹌折屐、謝安折屐、圍棋賭墅、東山再起，全部出自這一役及其前後；它同時成為中國軍事史上以少勝多的樣板與反面教材——凡是好戰而輕率、輕視內部裂痕而驕於新勝的征服者，都可以在這裡找到自己的鏡子；而南方則因這場勝利換來數十年安寧，直到420年劉裕篡晉，南朝的國祚才告一段落。
impactEn: The consequences of Fei River went far beyond the result of a single battle. First of all it changed the balance of power between north and south. The Eastern Jin followed up its victory with northern expeditions, recovered for a time the old lands south of the Yellow River, and drove its arms as far as Ba and Tong; but with Xie An and then Xie Xuan dead or withdrawn, and with the campaigns of Huan Wen and Liu Yu draining the resources of the Jin, the old pattern of stalemate between north and south returned. Second, the Former Qin came apart within two years. Back in Chang'an Fu Jian listened to slander and had Wang Tong and Fu Fang killed; in 385 Yao Chang killed him; the north broke up into Later Qin, Later Yan, Western Qin, Dai and others, and only when the Northern Wei reunited the north in 439 was the road to the reunification of the country by Sui in 589 made level. In the meantime the north passed through nearly sixty years of the Sixteen Kingdoms, and Han and non-Han populations were mixed again and again by war and by forced migration, so that the fusion of peoples accelerated; the antagonism between the Guanzhong and the Shandong groups that runs through Sui and Tang, and the Guanzhong-Luoyang axis itself, both have their roots in these decades. Institutionally the Northern Depot troops became the finest armed force of the Southern dynasties; both Liu Laozhi and Liu Yu rose on them, the military system of the south took its shape, and the armed power of the Huan clan of Jingzhou was spent to the last in the hands of Huan Xuan. Culturally, the battle produced the densest cluster of idioms in the Chinese language: throwing the whips to sever the current, every tree and bush a soldier, the wind and the cranes, the staggering feet that broke the wooden clogs, Xie An breaking the teeth of his clogs, the game of go staked against a house, and the eastern hill rising again. All of them come from this battle and what surrounded it. The battle is at once the model and the warning of Chinese military history for defeating a larger enemy with fewer: every conqueror who was war-happy and careless, who disregarded the fissures inside his own camp and grew proud of an easy victory, can find his own mirror here. The south, on the other hand, bought itself decades of peace with this victory, and did not lay that chapter down until Liu Yu took the throne from the Jin in 420 and the Southern dynasties began.
result: 結果是一場乾淨利落、又留下長尾的勝利。十一月淝水兩岸的決戰，晉軍以八萬北府兵等部擊潰秦軍二十餘萬前鋒：秦軍不戰自潰，自相蹈藉，蔽野塞川，屍首塞住淝水，逃回的士卒在飢凍與恐懼中死者十之七八，苻堅中流矢只帶少數人退回淮北，苻融戰死，壽陽收復；朱序等降將回到東晉，而戰前輕視謝安的桓沖不久之後慚愧而亡。軍事上晉軍大勝，但戰役的收尾並不完整：晉軍沒有追到淮北，沒有乘勢全殲秦軍主力，荊州方向姚萇所部被巴東守將與夏口的桓沖主力擋住，涼州兵與巴蜀兵更遠未至，苻堅的主力因此得以保全，前秦並非當場覆亡。取勝的關鍵有三：洛澗夜襲先破秦軍一萬五千人，奪其銳氣；隔水對峙時的請退之策誘使秦軍自行崩亂；以及朱序在關鍵時刻的喊話與秦將之間對方略的分裂。苻堅自己也歎「悔不聽王景略陽平公之言」，追憶王猛的警告。前秦並未在淝水之後立即覆亡：苻堅回關中後平定內亂、重新集兵，兩年後才被姚萇殺死，帝國崩潰的過程又延續了兩年。而對東晉來說，這場勝利換來的是數十年的南安，劉牢之隨即北伐收復洛陽，桓溫、劉裕先後北伐，最終把東晉的國祚送到420年劉裕手中。
resultEn: The result was a victory that was clean and swift, and that left a long tail behind it. In the eleventh month, in the decision on the banks of the Fei, the Jin army of some 80,000 Northern Depot troops and the rest broke the Qin vanguard of more than 200,000: the Qin broke up without a battle, trampled one another, the dead covered the field and dammed the stream, and of the men who fled, seven or eight in ten perished of hunger, cold and fear. Fu Jian was hit by an arrow and retreated north of the Huai with a few men, Fu Rong was killed, and Shouyang was retaken. The surrendered officers such as Zhu Xu came back to the Jin, and Huan Chong, who had held the Xie family in contempt before the battle, died shortly after in shame. Militarily the Jin won outright, but the campaign was not tidied up. The Jin did not pursue to the north bank of the Huai, did not destroy the main body of the Qin host, the Liang and Yi troops of Yao Chang were held up by the Jin commander at Badong and by Huan Chong's main force at Xiakou, and the Liangzhou and Bashu troops were further away still and had not arrived. Fu Jian's main army was thus preserved, and the Former Qin did not perish on the field. Three things decided the day: the night attack at Luojian, which cost the Qin fifteen thousand men and took the edge off them; the request to withdraw, which set the Qin army tumbling into disorder of its own accord; and the shout of Zhu Xu at the critical moment, together with the divisions among the Qin generals over their own plan. Fu Jian himself lamented that he had not listened to the words of Wang Meng, the Lord of Yangping, and looked back on the minister's warning. The Former Qin did not collapse immediately after Fei River: Fu Jian returned to Guanzhong, put down the disorders within, and gathered his soldiers again, and it was two years later that Yao Chang killed him, so that the process of the empire's dissolution ran on for a further two years. For the Eastern Jin, the victory bought decades of peace in the south; Liu Laozhi at once campaigned north and recovered Luoyang, Huan Wen and Liu Yu campaigned north in their turn, and in the end the life of the Eastern Jin was carried to the year 420, when Liu Yu took the throne.
